title: Glazed salmon over rice

items: 2 salmon fillets (6 oz each, about 1 inch thick), skin on or off
8 oz asparagus, woody ends snapped off, or 8 oz green beans, trimmed

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Start the rice now if it isn't already cooked.

Toss the asparagus or green beans with the olive oil and ¼ tsp salt on a rimmed sheet pan and spread in one layer. Roast asparagus 10–12 min or green beans 15–20 min, until tender and browned in spots.
While the vegetables roast, whisk the soy sauce, honey, sriracha and garlic in a small bowl. Pat the salmon dry and season with ¼ tsp salt.
Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the salmon, flesh-side down, and sear 3–4 min without moving, until golden and it releases easily.
Flip the salmon and turn the heat down to medium-low. Pour in the glaze. Honey burns quickly, so keep it at a gentle bubble.
Cook 3–4 min more, spooning the glaze over the fish, until the glaze is thick and sticky and the salmon reads 145°F in the thickest part or flakes easily with a fork.
Serve the salmon over rice with the vegetables. Spoon over any glaze left in the pan and sprinkle with scallions.
tips: If the glaze gets too thick before the fish is done, stir in 1 Tbsp water.
Cooking for 4? Double everything and sear the salmon in 2 batches, or use 2 skillets.
Air fryer: brush the salmon with half the glaze and air fry at 400°F for 8–10 min, to 145°F. Simmer the rest of the glaze 1–2 min in a small pan and spoon it over.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat gently in the microwave at 50% power 1–2 min, or eat it cold over rice. Cool cooked rice within 2 hr.
